lines: So, what did you think of the new apartment?
The location's great, and I love the kitchen.
Well, the rent is about two hundred dollars more than we agreed to spend. I'm just not sure we can stretch that far every month.
Hmm. Maybe we should keep looking, then.
items.question: Why is the man hesitant about the apartment?
choices: It is too far from their workplaces.
The kitchen is too small.
It is more expensive than their budget.
The landlord seems unfriendly.
items.explain_ja: 女性の But? は、何か問題があるんでしょう、という促しです。rent is about two hundred dollars more than we agreed to spend が、予算より高い、に言い換えられています。stretch は、お金をやりくりして無理をする、という意味です。

lines: Ms. Garcia, have you had a chance to review my report on the supplier contracts?
I skimmed it. It's thorough, but the conclusion section is a little thin.
Thin? I thought it summarized everything.
It summarizes, but it doesn't tell me what you'd actually recommend. That's what the board will want to see.
items.question: What does the woman want the man to do?
choices: Add clear recommendations to the conclusion.
Shorten the entire report.
Contact the suppliers again.
Present the report to the board himself.
items.explain_ja: thin は、内容が薄い、という意味です。it doesn't tell me what you'd actually recommend から、提案を加えてほしい、とわかります。skim は、ざっと目を通す、です。

lines: Dad, can I borrow the car this weekend? Jenny and I want to drive to the lake.
The lake? That's a three-hour drive, and you only got your license last month.
I'm sure you are. Tell you what, why don't I drive you both there, and you can take the wheel on the way back if the roads are quiet?
items.question: What does the father suggest?
choices: His daughter should go to a closer place.
They should take a bus to the lake.
Jenny should drive the whole way.
He will take them and let his daughter drive part of the way.
items.explain_ja: Tell you what は、こうしよう、という提案の前置きです。take the wheel は、運転する、という意味です。行きは父が運転し、帰りは娘が運転する、という提案です。
keys: じゃあこうしよう（提案の前置き）

lines: Did you finish the novel I lent you?
Only halfway? I couldn't put it down.
To be honest, I found the main character hard to sympathize with. I kept waiting for something to happen, and it never really did.
items.question: What does the woman think about the novel?
choices: It was too short.
It was exciting from start to finish.
It was slow and not very engaging.
It was difficult to understand because of its vocabulary.
items.explain_ja: I kept waiting for something to happen, and it never really did が、展開が遅くて退屈、という意味です。男性の couldn't put it down は、夢中で読むのをやめられなかった、なので、二人の感想は反対です。
keys: 夢中で読むのをやめられなかった

lines: Excuse me, I bought this jacket here last week, and the zipper is already broken.
I'm sorry about that. Do you have your receipt?
Thank you. Unfortunately, we're out of that size in this color, but I can either give you a full refund or order one from another branch. It would take about a week.
I need it for a trip on Friday, so I'll take the money back.
items.question: What will the woman do?
choices: Wait for a new jacket to be ordered.
Choose a jacket in a different color.
Get her money back.
Have the zipper repaired.
items.explain_ja: I'll take the money back が、get her money back、つまり返金を受ける、です。金曜日に必要なので、1週間かかる取り寄せは選びませんでした。

lines: Have you heard? They're moving our department to the new building downtown.
Really? That'll add forty minutes to my commute.
Apparently, they're offering a transportation allowance.
That's something, I suppose. But money won't give me those forty minutes back.
items.question: How does the woman feel about the move?
choices: She is pleased about the allowance.
She plans to quit her job.
She wants to work in the new building.
She is unhappy about the longer commute.
items.explain_ja: That's something, I suppose は、ないよりはまし、という消極的な評価です。その後の but が本音で、通勤時間が長くなることへの不満を表しています。

lines: Doctor, my back has been hurting for about two weeks now.
Have you been doing anything different lately? Lifting heavy things, perhaps?
Not really. Although I did start working from home, and I've been using the kitchen table as a desk.
That might explain it. Before we consider any medication, I'd look at your chair and screen height.
items.question: What does the doctor think?
choices: The woman needs strong pain medicine.
The woman's work setup may be causing the pain.
The woman injured her back lifting something.
The woman should stop working from home.
items.explain_ja: That might explain it は、それが原因かもしれない、という意味です。薬より先に、椅子と画面の高さを見直すよう勧めています。work setup は、仕事の環境、という言い換えです。
keys: それが原因かもしれない

lines: I'm thinking of signing up for that marathon in April.
A full marathon? You've never run more than five kilometers.
I've got five months to train.
Well, if you're serious, you might want to start with the half marathon in February and see how your body handles it.
items.question: What does the woman suggest?
choices: The man should give up running.
The man should try a shorter race first.
The man should run the marathon in February.
The man should train with a coach.
items.explain_ja: you might want to は、〜したほうがいいかもね、という柔らかい提案です。the half marathon が、shorter race に言い換えられています。
keys: 〜するといいかもしれない（柔らかい提案）

lines: Jim, the client called. She wants the presentation moved up to Monday.
Monday? We were planning on Wednesday. The design team hasn't even finished the slides.
I know. I told her it'd be tight, but she has a board meeting on Tuesday.
Then I guess we're working this weekend. I'll let the design team know.
items.question: What will the man probably do?
choices: Ask the client to keep the Wednesday date.
Cancel the presentation.
Work over the weekend to meet the new deadline.
Attend the client's board meeting.
items.explain_ja: move up は、予定を早める、という意味です。put off、延期する、の反対です。Then I guess we're working this weekend から、週末に作業して間に合わせることがわかります。

lines: The chef was entertaining, but we spent most of the time watching him rather than cooking.
That's not really a class, then, is it?
Exactly. For that price, I expected to get my hands dirty. I'll look for something more practical next time.
items.question: What was the woman's complaint about the cooking class?
choices: The chef was not entertaining.
It did not give students enough hands-on practice.
The kitchen was not clean.
It was cheaper than she expected.
items.explain_ja: get my hands dirty は、実際に手を動かす、という意味です。見ているだけで実習が少なかった、という不満を、hands-on practice と言い換えています。
